issues.description: Backslash-separated traversal (e.g. '..\\WEB-INF\\web.xml') bypasses the re-screen: unpatched forFile only splits on '/', so it yields resource path '/..\\WEB-INF\\web.xml' which the ^(web|meta)-inf anchored regex does not match; on Windows getRealPath then traverses to the protected file. This is precisely the class the official forFile separator-normalization fix closes, and it survives our patch.

Fix is applied only at ContextAssetRequestHandler; the shared sink forFile (AbstractResource) and other Resource callers reaching file sinks remain unprotected, so overlap with the official fix location is zero.
Mitigation is a start-anchored WEB-INF/META-INF blocklist rather than canonicalize-and-contain-within-base-dir, the CWE-022 defense-of-record; fragile to separator/encoding variants.

POV did not reproduce before the patch (pov_before_reproduced=false) and no regression tests were executed (regressions_ran=0), so both effectiveness against the real vector and absence of regressions are only weakly evidenced.

result.summary: Our patch adds a post-resolution re-screen in ContextAssetRequestHandler that catches forward-slash '../WEB-INF' traversal after forFile collapses the '..' segments, and it is a tight, low-risk change. However, it does not address the vulnerability's actual root cause: the official fix normalizes backslash-to-forward-slash inside AbstractResource.forFile so that Windows-style '..\\WEB-INF' segments are collapsed and screened uniformly. Because our patch leaves forFile untouched and relies on a start-anchored WEB-INF/META-INF blocklist, a backslash payload resolves to '/..\\WEB-INF\\web.xml', evades the regex, and remains exploitable on Windows. It is therefore a weaker subset of the official fix that closes only one variant at one call site.
result.root_cause: forFile() splits relative paths only on '/', so backslash-separated '..' segments are never normalized or collapsed and slip past the WEB-INF/META-INF screen to reach getRealPath, enabling path traversal on the shared resource-resolution sink.
